 Togo Football Chief Accuses Algeria of Neglecting Team at Airport
 A four-hour wait, exhausted players sleeping on airport seats, and no federation officials in sight have sparked complaints from Togo's football chief.
 by Ikram Srahna 
 Nov, 16, 2026

 Rabat – An overnight delay at Algiers’ Houari Boumediene Airport has prompted accusations against the Algerian Football Federation (FAF), with Togolese Football Federation President Guy Kossi Akpovy criticizing the treatment of his country’s national team after Saturday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier. 
 Togo suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to Algeria on Saturday at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium in Tizi Ouzou, where Ramy Bensebaini scored the only goal in the 76th minute. 
 But Akpovy’s frustration extended beyond the result on the pitch. 
 Speaking to Algerian sports outlet Compétition, the Togolese football chief accused the FAF of failing to provide adequate assistance to his delegation during its departure from Algeria. 
 “What bothered us a little was our departure for Lomé. We arrived at the airport very early. We had a special flight that we paid for, and the state paid for that plane so that we could return under the best possible conditions,” he explained. 
 “But what is frustrating is that nobody made the necessary arrangements. I didn’t even see a single member of the [Algerian] federation. This is not normal.” 
 According to Akpovy, the chartered aircraft was already at the airport at 2 a.m., and the Togolese delegation arrived an hour later. However, the team did not depart until 7 a.m.

 He described the four-hour wait as unnecessary and criticized the lack of communication surrounding the departure procedures. 
 “They kept us waiting for nothing. I saw members of our delegation sleeping on the airport seats. This is not normal,” he said. 
 Akpovy also claimed that airport personnel appeared uncertain about the arrangements. 
 “Even the airport staff didn’t know exactly what was going to happen. Frankly, we’re angry,” he added. 
 Despite his dissatisfaction, the Togolese official indicated that his federation would not subject Algeria’s delegation to similar treatment when the teams meet again. 
 The allegations have emerged just before Tuesday’s return fixture in Lomé, where Togo will host Algeria at the Kégué Stadium in the fourth round of the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. 
 Algeria currently lead Group I with seven points from three matches, while Togo sit third with three points. 
 The Algerian Football Federation has not publicly responded to Akpovy’s accusations.
